item.title: Argos expands marketplace to 130,000 products in biggest range push
item.description:
Argos plans to offer more than 130,000 products from vetted third‑party retailers and brands on its Trusted Sellers marketplace by the end of 2026. The platform, which was trialled with 40 partners in July, already offers more than 70,000 products. The expansion marks the biggest increase in Argos’s product range in its history.
Initially focused on furniture, home, and toys, Trusted Sellers is now expanding into health and beauty, gifting and electricals, with beauty brands such as Clarins, Dermalogica, and Medicube already available. Products are delivered directly by Trusted Sellers, although customers can still earn Nectar Points on marketplace purchases. The expansion forms part of a wider transformation programme at Argos that includes investment in its digital experience, rapid delivery, Argos Pay, and other customer propositions. Every partner is vetted by Argos before joining Trusted Sellers, ensuring that products meet the retailer’s quality and safety standards.
“The launch of Trusted Sellers enables us to complement those ranges with thousands of new lines from brands and independent businesses that mean our customers get an even wider range,” Graham Biggart said.
In July, Argos trialled the Trusted Sellers marketplace with 40 partners, offering over 70,000 products. The expansion comes after Sainsbury’s agreed to sell Argos to Swift Partners for £120 million in July, ending ten years of ownership since acquiring the brand for £1.4 billion in 2016. Graham Biggart said the feedback on and from Trusted Sellers has been incredibly positive.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/argos-marketplace-range-push)

item.title: Xeneta says Hormuz freight shock may have peaked after 344% rate surge
item.description:
Xeneta reported that container rates from China to the U.S. East and West Coasts have risen 344 percent and 335 percent since February 28, but the market has likely reached its post‑Hormuz crisis peak. The spread between the two coasts has widened to $3,177 per 40‑foot equivalent unit, with East‑Coast bound containers averaging $11,523 and West‑Coast bound boxes averaging $8,346.
Xeneta forecasts that, looking three months ahead, spot rates could fall to $6,000‑$7,000 for East‑Coast destinations and $4,500‑$5,500 for the West Coast. The UAE’s National Association of Freight and Logistics notes that moving cargo into the Persian Gulf now costs three to five times pre‑war levels due to surcharges, rerouting and land‑transport expenses. Maritime security sources recorded at least 12 attacks on oil, LNG and LPG tankers in the week of September 28 to October 5, the highest weekly total since the conflict began. The International Maritime Organization separately verified nine of those incidents, up from a previous weekly high of eight in mid‑July.
“We can say with a level of confidence that the market has reached its post-Hormuz crisis peak in 2026,” Peter Sand, chief analyst at ocean and air freight benchmarking platform Xeneta said.
“The spread will narrow as the broader decline takes hold in the remainder of the year, driven mainly by a harder fall into the U.S. East Coast due to its more elevated starting point,” Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta said.
Before the Hormuz crisis, the cost gap between East and West Coast shipments was just $772 per 40‑foot unit. In the week of July 13, maritime logs recorded eight vessel attacks, the prior peak.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/strait-of-hormuz-freight-rates-peaked-iran-war-xeneta-container-shipping-oil-1239320306)

item.title: Report urges brands to build farmer ties for better cotton traceability
item.description:
Ani Wells and Anne Oudard released the fourth installment of their five-year #WhoMadeMyCotton investigation on World Cotton Day, arguing that cotton traceability requires brands to know the farmers who grow it. Even with certified cotton backed by transaction certificates, tracing the fiber back through the supply chain took hours of painstaking investigation.
Gins pay farmers or intermediaries for cotton and hold essential origin data, but their records often lack a standardized format unless they operate within a certified cotton system. Without standardized gin data, information rarely travels downstream, forcing brands to undertake large-scale, unrealistic investigations to trace cotton to its source. The report recommends that brands build lasting relationships with farming communities and the wider network of field workers, input suppliers, agronomists and local traders to obtain full traceability.
“Farmers don’t operate in isolation,” Anne Oudard, former designer and lead of sourcing and supply chain at Cotton Diaries said.
“The information doesn’t get passed on, and so when at the end of the supply chain you want to retrieve this information, you have to go through a massive investigation that is unrealistic at scale,” Anne Oudard, former designer and lead of sourcing and supply chain at Cotton Diaries said.
The #WhoMadeMyCotton investigation started five years ago to map the origins of cotton used in denim, and this report marks its fourth step. The project relies on field visits and conversations in Brazil, India and Turkey to gather insights.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sj-denim/who-made-your-cotton-1239319748)

item.title: Evans Transportation warns excess 3PL use drives up freight rates
item.description:
Evans Transportation, which serves roughly 300 customers, warned that shippers relying on multiple third‑party logistics providers for the same lane may see carriers delay loads and push rates up. He noted that Gulf Coast load‑to‑truck ratios have reached hundreds of loads per truck, a condition that could worsen with an approaching tropical storm.
Conrad described the phenomenon as “broker poker,” explaining that when many 3PLs bid on the same lane carriers learn to hold out for higher payments. He said Evans Transportation retains other 3PLs only when a shipper already has a vetted partner on a given segment, rather than displacing long‑standing relationships. The firm’s managed transportation model combines proprietary technology, off‑the‑shelf tools and an agentic AI voice system that fields initial inbound calls before passing them to live staff.
“Those brokers who are going out to the marketplace over and over and over again on the same lane, they’re driving the rate up because the carriers get smart and they say, I’m going to wait for a little while because you guys are all bidding on it,” John Conrad, Chief Revenue Officer at Evans Transportation Services said.
Evans Transportation describes its managed transportation approach as “outsourcing done right,” combining proprietary technology with off‑the‑shelf tools and, most recently, an agentic AI voice system to handle initial inbound call volume. The company, founded in 1985 and privately held, serves roughly 300 customers and holds an MC number beginning with 1.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/why-adding-3pls-can-backfire-on-shippers)

item.title: Hurricane Isaias threatens Gulf refineries as it nears Category 3 strength
item.description:
Hurricane Isaias, currently a Category 1 storm, is forecast to reach Category 3 with winds up to 100 mph before making landfall Friday around 2 p.m., threatening Gulf Coast refineries and ports. Gulf State refineries in the storm’s path represent half of the nation’s refining capacity, or 18.2 million barrels per day.
Tender rejections in New Orleans, Mobile, and Montgomery are already running between 17% and 19%, above national averages, as shippers move freight ahead of the storm. Rainfall of 3 to 6 inches is expected across the region, with isolated totals possibly reaching 10 inches, raising flood concerns for inland routes. The Ports of Mobile and New Orleans lie in the projected impact zone, while FEMA staging sites in Jacksonville and Atlanta could spur emergency freight demand after landfall.
“I do not play about the weather,” Malcolm Harris, who provided the meteorological analysis said.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/hurricane-isaias-category-3-threat-to-gulf-supply-chain)

item.title: OFAC warns CFOs that sanctions risk can lurk in payment routes
item.description:
On Monday (Oct. 5), the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control warned foreign financial institutions that continuing to transact with sanctioned entities could expose them to sanctions at any time without notice. The warning came as global supply chain pressures reached a four‑month high, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s GSCPI released Tuesday (Oct. 6).
OFAC pointed to recent actions against banks that gave sanctioned actors such as Iran access to correspondent banking and the international financial system. Specifically, the agency cited its August move to cut U.S. correspondent banking access for Banque Misr UAE, its September designation of Turkey‑based Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries, and its action against Russia’s VTB Bank for Iranian sanctions evasion. Correspondent banking lets a regional bank without direct currency access move money through a partner institution, a link that can become blocked if the intermediary is sanctioned.
“The term ‘cross‑border’ signifies that a payment traverses different legal entities, jurisdictions, regulatory frameworks, sanction regimes,” Emanuela Saccarola, Citi’s head of cross-border payments and services said.
Traditional sanctions controls are heavily counterparty-centric: Who are we paying? Who owns the business? Is the company or its beneficial owner sanctioned? Is the destination permitted. The implication is bigger than freezing the assets of a sanctioned company.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/cross-border-payments/2026/ofac-warning-shows-cfos-sanctions-risk-can-hide-in-the-payment-route)

item.title: Lululemon CEO Heidi O’Neill names new CPO and COO as part of C-suite overhaul
item.description:
About a month after joining Lululemon, CEO Heidi O’Neill appointed former Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger as chief product officer and ex‑Walmart Canada growth chief Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer, with the new roles set to start Oct. 26. Simultaneously, Lululemon said chief supply chain officer Ted Dagnese and chief brand and product activation officer Nikki Neuburger will depart effective Nov. 6, while the company searches to fill three additional C‑suite posts — chief brand officer, chief communications officer, and chief technology officer.
The product and operations roles are newly created positions within Lululemon’s executive team. O’Neill said the reshaped leadership will work more cohesively around strategy and execution to deliver greater impact for guests, communities, and the business. She emphasized putting product, design, and innovation at the center of operations to build a stronger pipeline of differentiated offerings for both stores and online channels. The appointments were announced roughly one month after O’Neill assumed the CEO role, marking her first executive reshuffle. Lululemon said it is actively seeking candidates for chief brand officer, chief communications officer, and chief technology officer to complete the leadership team.
“Lululemon is a rare, extraordinary brand, but we have work to do to build a stronger and more competitive company,” Heidi O’Neill said.
“We are establishing a deeply experienced leadership team that will work in a more coordinated manner, aligned around the strategy and execution that delivers the most impact for our guests, our communities, and our business,” Heidi O’Neill said.
O’Neill began her tenure as Lululemon’s CEO in April, and industry watchers had been anticipating her initial leadership decisions. The announcement was described as the first step in addressing the company’s recent performance challenges.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/lululemon-ceo-heidi-oneill-overhauls-c-suite-first-move/832434)

item.title: ICSC Projects $1.7 Trillion Holiday Spend, 78% to Match or Top 2025 Levels
item.description:
The ICSC projected that holiday retail sales will reach $1.7 trillion this season, forecasting growth of 4.3 to 4.9 percent. The survey found that 78 percent of consumers intend to spend the same or more than last year, while the top 10 percent anticipate spending five times the average shopper.
About 23 percent of respondents said they expect to still be paying for their holiday purchases in 2027. Nearly two‑thirds (68 percent) said discounts, promotions and exclusive offers will encourage additional store trips, and 93 percent plan to visit a physical store to buy or pick up an online order. Meanwhile, 61 percent said they will use AI tools or assistants this year, up from 47 percent in the prior survey.
“Consumers have made it clear they are willing to make sacrifices for the things that matter to them this holiday season, but they are making careful decisions about when and where they spend to make that money go further,” Tom McGee, president and CEO of the ICSC said.
Last year’s survey found 47 percent of consumers planned to use AI tools for holiday shopping, compared with 61 percent this year. Concerns about the job market affecting holiday spending rose from 43 percent in 2025 to 49 percent in the current poll.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/shoppers-prioritize-holiday-despite-financial-strain-1239319045)

item.title: IMC Logistics orders 50 Tesla Semis for California drayage fleet
item.description:
IMC Logistics announced on September 22 that it will add 50 Tesla Semi trucks to its California fleet. The order will place Standard Range models, rated for 325 miles, in port drayage and Long Range models, rated for 500 miles, on lanes between Southern California and inland destinations.
IMC did not disclose how many of each model it ordered or when all 50 trucks will enter service. The trucks will augment an existing mixed fleet that already includes battery-electric, hydrogen fuel-cell and renewable-diesel vehicles, including Volvo battery-electric trucks and 50 Nikola hydrogen fuel-cell trucks purchased in March 2024. Tesla’s Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada, has a 1.7‑million‑square‑foot footprint and is designed to produce up to 50,000 trucks per year.
“The addition of 50 Tesla Semis strengthens that strategy as well as allows IMC to establish zero-emission service for long haul lanes,” Jim Gillis, Pacific Region president at IMC Logistics said.
“The future of trucking is likely a mix of diesel, electric, and hydrogen, each solving different problems,” Brian Kobza, chief commercial officer at IMC Logistics said.
WattEV ordered 370 Tesla Semis in May to run from its charging stations at the Port of Oakland and Fresno, with the first 50 due in 2026 and full deployment by the end of 2027. In September, Tesla was named primary manufacturer on a 2,500‑truck electric order through ZET SCALE, a shipper‑carrier alliance whose founding shippers include Microsoft and PepsiCo. Los Angeles is among the 10 freight hubs that the ZET SCALE order targets first.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/imc-logistics-tesla-semi-order)

item.title: UPS cuts seasonal hiring by 9% as package volume falls 3.3%
item.description:
UPS announced it will hire about 9% fewer seasonal workers this year compared with last year, according to a Reuters report. The company also said it reduced its seasonal workforce by 15,000 positions in 2025, according to its annual report.
UPS’s U.S. average daily package volume fell 3.3% year-over-year in the second quarter, as the company completed its planned cut of lower‑yielding Amazon business. Revenue per package rose 9.3% over the same period, driven by higher prices and a more profitable customer mix. The firm’s global workforce stands at roughly 460,000 employees, according to its own release. The seasonal hiring cut is part of UPS’s broader strategy to reduce shipments for Amazon and focus on more profitable deliveries.
“the company is attempting to rebuild the economics of parcel delivery around a different formula of less low-return volume, more automation, and a technology layer that makes its physical network visible and adaptable in real time,” UPS CEO Carol Tomé, CEO said.
Last year UPS hired more than 125,000 seasonal workers for the holiday season, according to an October 2024 company article. In its 2025 annual report, the company reported cutting 15,000 seasonal positions for that year.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/shipping/2026/ups-trims-seasonal-hiring-after-planned-package-volume-reduction)

item.title: Ramp veterans raise $25 million for AI creative platform Melius
item.description:
Ramp veterans Joowon Kim, Young Kim, and Arnav Ramu announced on Oct. 6 that they have raised $25 million for their AI creative platform Melius. The financing will support expansion of Melius’s platform, which lets users generate images, videos and ad campaigns using AI agents. Joowon Kim, Young Kim and Arnav Ramu previously worked as engineers at the spending/finance software company Ramp.
After six months of building an AI-powered performance marketing tool, the team decided the idea lacked traction and scrapped the entire codebase. Melius now offers a set of AI agents that handle tasks such as adjusting lighting so users can focus on creative direction. The platform targets people who want to move from concept to finished creative assets without a steep learning curve.
“Transitioning from wanting to make something to actually making it has never been seamless,” Joowon Kim, Co-Founder said.
“We scrapped the entire codebase; we burned all of it,” Joowon Kim, Co-Founder said.
Before raising the $25 million, the founders had spent six months developing an AI-powered performance marketing tool that they ultimately abandoned. They then shifted focus to building a platform for creating images, videos and ad campaigns using AI agents.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/ramp-veterans-raise-25-million-for-ai-creative-platform-melius)

item.title: Pacsun uses TikTok creator to sell 11,000 jeans in 48 hours
item.description:
In November 2023, Pacsun sold 11,000 pairs of its Casey Jean in Astrid Wash after a TikTok video by creator Lyla Biggs went viral two days before Black Friday. The brand said the surge generated over $20 million in sales on TikTok alone.
Biggs, who had roughly 5,000 followers at the time, is a member of Pacsun’s TikTok affiliate creator program. Pacsun, founded in 1980 as a surf shop, now markets to Gen Z and Gen Alpha shoppers. The video featured the low‑rise Casey Jean in Astrid Wash, a style that helped the brand capture a sudden spike in demand.
“Brands are going to make the mistake of believing the attention economy is about capturing more attention, and it is not,” Kim Vernon, marketing veteran formerly of Calvin Klein and Prada Group said.
The panel occurred at Impakt, an invite‑only business conference in New York City on a Tuesday. Panelists including Channing Bailey of Channing & Company, brand strategist Christine Keeley, and Vylit co‑founder Ami Gan echoed the need to find the right community amid a crowded market. The conversation occurred weeks before Black Friday, when U.S. online shoppers spent $11.8 billion the previous year according to Adobe Analytics.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/impakt-conference-attention-economy-brands-1239317672)

item.title: Port of Savannah handles record 504,000 TEUs in September
item.description:
The Georgia Ports Authority reported that the Port of Savannah moved more than 504,000 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo in September, setting a monthly record. September volumes rose 3.7% year-over-year, while the first quarter of the fiscal year totaled 1.5 million TEUs, up 2.7% and marking the port’s second‑best quarter ever.
The Appalachian Regional Port, the inland rail terminal linking Savannah to Northwest Georgia, saw a 13% rise in cargo volumes during the same first‑quarter period. Georgia Ports Authority attributed the September gain to a 5.5% year‑over‑year increase in imports, stronger consumer spending and an extended peak season that shifted Asian typhoon‑related delays into September. The authority also pointed to its $1.6 billion Ocean Terminal renovation, now 60% complete, which is projected to lift the terminal’s capacity from 200,000 to 1.75 million TEUs upon completion. The authority said the renovation is expected to provide an additional boost in the months ahead as the terminal’s capacity expands. The October 7 release from the Georgia Ports Authority disclosed the September figures and the year‑over‑year percentage increase.
“This September performance speaks volumes about our team and shows Georgia Ports is the key gateway to Georgia and the Southeast,” Alec Poitevint, chairman, Georgia Ports Authority said.
The port's first-quarter fiscal year total reached 1.5 million TEUs, up 2.7% year-over-year. That figure marked the port's second-best quarter in its history.
Source: SupplyChainBrain (https://supplychainbrain.com/articles/44979-port-of-savannah-logs-record-cargo-volumes-in-september)

item.title: Zim raises 2026 profit forecast 72% on strong demand
item.description:
Zim Integrated Shipping Services raised its full-year 2026 earnings guidance on Oct. 6, increasing the midpoint of its adjusted operating earnings outlook by 72%. The carrier now expects adjusted EBITDA of $2.7 billion to $3.0 billion, up from the previous range of $2.0 billion to $2.4 billion.
At the midpoint, the outlook puts adjusted EBITDA at $2.85 billion, an increase of $650 million or roughly 30%. Adjusted EBIT is projected at $1.4 billion to $1.7 billion, compared with the earlier forecast of $700 million to $1.1 billion. The revised forecast is issued while Zim waits for its pending acquisition by Hapag-Lloyd to close. Zim cited continued strong market demand and favorable momentum in freight rates as reasons for the upgrade. The announcement did not provide updated cargo-volume projections or quantify how much of the increase reflected rates versus shipment demand. Zim noted uncertainty surrounding the transaction, geopolitical instability and fluctuations in freight rates, vessel supply and shipping demand as factors that could cause actual results to differ from projections. The guidance uses adjusted financial measures rather than results prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards. The company warned that adjusted EBITDA excludes debt-service and capital outlays and should not be considered cash available to the firm.
In August, Zim had issued an initial 2026 earnings guidance range of $2.0 billion to $2.4 billion for adjusted EBITDA and $700 million to $1.1 billion for adjusted EBIT. Both comparisons are measured against the company’s Aug. 19 forecast for the year ending Dec. 31.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/zim-lifts-profit-forecast-72-on-strong-demand)

item.title: U.S. diesel averages $6.20 a gallon as freight rates beat nine‑year norms
item.description:
U.S. on‑highway diesel averaged $6.20 a gallon on Oct. 5, down from $6.38 a week earlier according to the Energy Information Administration. For the week beginning Sept. 13, national spot freight rates were 20% above nine‑year seasonal averages for dry vans, 28% for refrigerated trailers and 25% for flatbeds, per DAT data reported by Trucking Dive. Trailer orders climbed to 24,144 units in August, a 43% jump from July, according to FTR data cited by Trucking Dive.
Dry van rates slipped three cents to $2.17 per mile while refrigerated rates gained two cents to $2.73 and flatbed rates fell two cents to $2.60 nationally, even as bellwether state rates rose six cents. Loads posted on DAT One rose 16% to 2.9 million during the week of Sept. 13, outpacing an 8% increase in truck postings and pushing load‑to‑truck ratios higher across all major equipment types. North Dakota’s Sept. 29 emergency order lets agricultural vehicles use tax‑free red‑dyed diesel on public roads, potentially saving eligible users 19 cents a gallon in state taxes through Nov. 30, while Texas has eased similar restrictions. Load‑to‑truck ratios increased for dry van, refrigerated and flatbed segments, but the holiday‑shortened prior week clouds whether the rise signals a lasting trend.
“It is a help, but it is not a solution,” Cherri Harris, CEO and owner of Swint Logistics Group said.
“energy prices are likely to stay elevated until shipping through the Strait of Hormuz becomes more predictable and more refining capacity returns,” Eimear Bonner, CFO of Chevron said.
Although diesel prices have slipped recently, freight expenses continue to squeeze finance teams. Freight rates still sit above their typical seasonal norms. A proposed Oct. 1 trucker work stoppage has added further uncertainty to an already tight freight market.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/diesels-supply-crunch-may-hit-cfos-through-freight-contracts/831981)

item.title: Experts explore trusted data and AI for autonomous supply chains
item.description:
On Tuesday, November 17, HERE Technologies, DCSA and AWS invited supply chain professionals to a discussion on moving beyond visibility toward autonomous, AI-driven operations. The session highlighted that billions have been invested in supply chain visibility yet disruptions, delays and manual intervention remain a daily reality.
Participants learned that the next challenge is creating data and insights trustworthy enough to trigger automated actions without human review. Discussions covered how trusted data, predictive ETAs and location intelligence form the foundation for proactive orchestration across multimodal networks. Industry standards and ecosystem collaboration were presented as essential for enabling end-to-end visibility and consistent event data sharing. The panel also examined how disruption signals can be converted into intelligent decisions and automated responses through AI-powered recommendations. The conversation also noted that standardized events and trusted ETAs are prerequisites for moving from reactive tracking to predictive, autonomous operations. Panelists described what autonomous, AI-driven supply chains look like in practice, emphasizing continuous learning loops and real-time decision execution. The organizers aimed to explore how trusted data, industry standards and predictive intelligence can move supply chains beyond visibility toward proactive orchestration.
Before the event, supply chain leaders had poured billions into visibility tools, yet many still faced frequent delays and required manual workarounds. As AI and automation investments grew, the focus shifted from merely collecting data to ensuring its reliability for decision‑making.
Source: SupplyChainBrain (https://supplychainbrain.com/articles/44982-from-visibility-to-autonomy-the-next-evolution-of-supply-chains)

item.title: Logistics firms agree to pay $2 million to settle hiring‑discrimination cases
item.description:
The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission announced on Monday that Birchstone Management will pay $500,000 and Mile Hi Companies $1.5 million to resolve federal hiring‑discrimination claims. Birchstone’s $500,000 settlement includes a $55,000 payment to the woman who filed the charge and a $445,000 fund for other affected applicants, while Mile Hi’s $1.5 million resolves allegations of discrimination against Black, female and Afghan job seekers.
Birchstone must revise its hiring and recruitment policies, provide training to personnel involved in hiring at several locations, audit its employment recordkeeping annually and report to the EEOC for two years.
The Birchstone settlement follows a Sept. 25 announcement that Mile Hi Companies agreed to pay $1.5 million to settle an EEOC lawsuit filed in 2024. The EEOC alleged Mile Hi denied employment opportunities to Black, female and Afghan applicants beginning in 2015.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/logistics-firms-to-pay-2m-to-settle-hiring-discrimination-cases)

item.title: Noah secures $38 million seed funding after 538% revenue surge
item.description:
Noah closed a $38 million seed round after raising an additional $16 million from new and existing investors, building on $22 million raised earlier in 2025, according to a Wednesday press release. Year‑to‑date revenue jumped 538% versus 2025 while the company added more than 150 new customers.
The proceeds will fund expansion of Noah’s international money‑transfer platform, including broadening its regulatory licences, hiring engineering and compliance specialists, and strengthening connections with local payment rails. In the United States, Noah will open a New York office to accelerate domestic growth and support its stablecoin‑based settlement services. Today the platform is live in over 150 markets, supports more than 60 currencies, and enables smooth cross‑border payments for enterprises and individuals both directly and through partnerships with fintechs, neobanks and workforce platforms. The company also highlighted recent integrations, noting that its infrastructure was adopted by the MiniPay wallet in October 2025 and that it has partnered with Cedar Money, Bron and Aurea Hub to broaden its service network.
“Noah is building the infrastructure that will make one-click international transactions possible everywhere, with full compliance at both the origination and destination of funds,” Shah Ramezani said.
“Just as neobanks have revolutionized domestic banking, we want to redefine global money transfer markets,” Shah Ramezani said.
In May, PYMNTS reported that a new architectural model of cross‑border settlement is emerging and is being powered by stablecoins. Earlier, Noah’s technology was integrated into the non‑custodial MiniPay wallet to enable freelancers, creators and sellers to receive global payouts.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/cryptocurrency/2026/stablecoin-rails-provider-noah-closes-38-million-dollar-seed-funding-following-538percent-revenue-surge)

item.title: France and Germany urge EU to adopt rapid-response trade tool
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that the EU’s trade deficit with China is expanding by about 1 billion euros per day. They urged the European Commission to create a rapid-response mechanism modeled on America’s Section 301 duties to counter unfair trade practices faster. They argued the EU’s current Anti‑Coercion Instrument requires a months‑long investigation and majority government approval before it can be used.
Macron and Merz said the EU’s trade deficit with China has reached roughly 1 billion euros ($1.125 billion) each day, driven by a surge of Chinese imports. European Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is set to travel to Beijing on Thursday for the final round of rebalancing talks that began four months ago, with outcomes to be reviewed at an EU leaders’ summit in Brussels on October 15‑16. The proposed rapid‑response tool would bypass the lengthy Anti‑Coercion Instrument process, allowing the Commission to act quickly without waiting for a months‑long probe or a unanimous member‑state vote. Macron and Merz also called on the Commission to diversify Europe’s supply chains to lessen dependence on Chinese goods.
“Without delaying the full use of the existing set of instruments, we need a comprehensive framework to complement our toolbox with new legal instruments—in a lean and non-bureaucratic way,” Emmanuel Macron, President of France, and Friedrich Merz, Chancellor of Germany said.
Days ahead of a scheduled EU‑China trade meeting, Macron and Merz warned that Chinese imports are threatening European manufacturers and the broader economy. They noted that US Section 301 tariffs have already redirected Chinese goods toward Europe, worsening the bloc’s imbalance.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/trade/france-germany-weapon-trade-threats-european-union-china-1239317928)

item.title: Amazon controls 63% of German online retail as sales hit €69.1bn
item.description:
Amazon held a 63 percent share of Germany’s online retail market in 2024, with its marketplace generating €69.1 billion in sales. The figure represents a 5 percent year‑on‑year increase, driven largely by third‑party sellers who contributed 46.1 percent of online spending while Amazon’s own retail accounted for 17.2 percent.
According to the IFH KÖln and General Evidence study, 97 percent of German online shoppers purchased from Amazon last year, and 59 percent of those shoppers were Prime members. Beyond online, Amazon accounted for 17 percent of total retail spending (online and offline) in the studied product categories and influenced an additional 24 percent of spending in those groups. The study also noted that Otto and Zalando together grew their German sales by €1.4 billion, while Shein and Temu saw combined growth of roughly €1 billion. One in eight Amazon shoppers said they are shifting some purchases to Chinese platforms, mainly for price reasons. Amazon continues to invest in its logistics network in the country, expanding fulfillment centers and delivery capabilities to support its growing sales volume.
IFH KÖln stresses that Amazon is facing somewhat stronger competition in Germany from Otto, Zalando, Shein and Temu. The researchers note that, although Amazon still leads on product range, ease of ordering and delivery speed, Chinese platforms are gaining ground on price.
Source: Ecommerce News Europe (https://ecommercenews.eu/amazon-holds-63-of-german-online-retail)

item.title: New trucking capacity remains stagnant as fleet growth stalls in August 2026
item.description:
As of October 2026, new for‑hire tractor counts stood at 19,520, showing no net increase despite elevated tender rejections. The SONAR Truckload Rejection Index lingered near 14%, roughly triple its 2023‑2025 average, while freight volume rose only 9% over the same period.
Net weekly authority additions exceeded 2,000 in August and September, marking a five‑year high, though much of the increase reflects administrative changes from the FMCSA’s Motus registration system rather than new trucks. Only about two‑thirds of new interstate registrants obtained liability insurance, a sharp drop from the over‑90% rate seen in 2019, indicating fewer carriers are actually hitting the road. A growing pool of disqualified drivers—202,345 CDL holders were in prohibited status as of January 2026—and stricter English‑language rules are raising entry costs and keeping new capacity out of the market. Overall for‑hire tractor fleets contracted by roughly 51,000 units in August alone, underscoring the speed at which existing capacity is exiting the market.
In the previous cycle (2020‑2022), rising rejection rates spurred a surge in new‑fleet tractors, which climbed to about 47,000 by mid‑2022. Before that, from 2019 to 2022, total operating authorities grew 51% while for‑hire tractors increased just 12%, showing a long‑standing gap between permissions and actual trucks. The current uptick in authority filings is largely driven by the Motus system clearing a backlog, not by genuine fleet expansion. The widening gap between authority issuance and actual truck purchases has been evident for years, but 2026’s administrative surge makes the disparity especially pronounced.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/is-trucking-capacity-coming-back-why-new-capacity-isnt-entering-the-2026-freight-market)

item.title: Former Flipkart executives seek ESOP buyback from Walmart amid IPO delay
item.description:
Former Flipkart executives Mukesh Bansal, Ankit Nagori and Sanjay Baweja urge Walmart to buy back their vested employee stock options, which currently allow only up to 5% liquidation under the July buyback tranche. The July buyback valued Flipkart at around $38.2 billion, but eligible employees could liquidate only a small fraction of their holdings.
The executives said they wrote to Walmart’s board, which includes Flipkart group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy, requesting a complete exit opportunity for their vested ESOPs granted 10 to 15 years ago. They argued that former employees should not be disadvantaged simply because they are no longer on Flipkart’s payroll and demanded fair treatment for the options. A Walmart spokesperson said the company would examine the issues raised and take the feedback seriously, while reiterating that an IPO remains part of the strategic roadmap when timing is right. For FY25, Flipkart Internet’s marketplace arm reported a 36.7% decline in consolidated net loss to ₹1,494.2 crore while total income rose 14% year-on-year to ₹20,807.4 crore.
Months earlier, Walmart completed the second tranche of Flipkart's employee stock buyback, valuing the company at about $38.2 billion and allowing employees to sell only up to 5% of their vested options. Walmart has said it aims for a $50 billion valuation before listing Flipkart, which has postponed its IPO to 2028 while focusing on profitability and expanding quick commerce.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/mukesh-bansal-ankit-nagori-seek-esop-buyback-from-flipkart-amid-ipo-uncertainty)

item.title: Lumio raises $12 million Series A to scale consumer electronics portfolio
item.description:
Lumio secured $12 million in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures, with Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital also participating. Founded in 2024 by former Xiaomi India CBO Raghu Reddy and ex-Flipkart executive Kailash Sankaranarayanan, the company launched its first smart TV lineup in early 2025 and now offers projectors and speakers. Lumio says it serves over 35,000 households across more than 5,000 pin codes and has crossed ₹100 crore in gross merchandise value within 13 months of commercial sales.
The fresh capital will be used to invest in product development, software enhancements, new category exploration, and to strengthen quality and after‑sales support as the business grows.
“This funding gives us the opportunity to invest further in our products and software, explore new categories, and strengthen quality and after-sales support as we grow,” Raghu Reddy said.
“India’s 3-3.5 Cr affluent households are reimagining their living rooms, and no longer default to legacy brands. Raghu and Kailash have leveraged their deep experience in home entertainment and customer insights to create a compelling home entertainment brand in Lumio,” Sajith Pai said.
Before the Series A, Lumio had raised a $4.3 million seed round in July 2024 from Stellaris Venture Partners, 3one4 Capital, Mamaearth’s Varun Alagh, Tracxn’s Abhishek Goyal and other angel investors.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/lumio-raises-12-mn-to-scale-consumer-electronics-portfolio)

item.title: Ikea launches second-hand marketplace in UK and Ireland for Family members
item.description:
Ikea has launched a second-hand marketplace in the UK and Ireland for Ikea Family members to buy and sell pre-owned Ikea products. Items listed on the marketplace cost on average 60% less than comparable new products.
Listing is free for Ikea Family members, who can receive payment either in cash or via an Ikea digital refund card that includes a 15% bonus. Sellers can scan eligible items to create listings that automatically add recommended prices, product images, measurements, descriptions, assembly instructions and care information. Mattresses, appliances, food, modified products, recalled products and any non-Ikea items are excluded from the marketplace.
“The way people furnish their homes has changed. Whether they are moving, redecorating or looking for a particular piece, more customers are considering pre-owned furniture alongside new and are actively searching for items that can help create a home that feels personal to them,” Greg Lucas said.
The marketplace already operates in eight European markets, including Spain, Norway, Portugal, Poland, Sweden and Belgium, with Germany set to join on 14 October. Ingka Group said the marketplace recorded 15 million visits and 95,700 listings across its first six markets up to 31 August 2026, with 25.5% of users being new or reactivated Ikea Family members.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/news/ikea-second-hand-marketplace-uk-ireland)

item.title: Wild Thingz gives shoppers at least 24 free Halloween sweets with Ocado purchase
item.description:
Wild Thingz launched a free Halloween sweets promotion with Ocado in October, offering shoppers at least 24 packets of sweets. Shoppers can claim the free bundle by uploading their Ocado receipt or delivery confirmation on the Wild Thingz website, with deliveries made while stocks last.
The free bundle consists of organic treat-size sweets that are plant-based and made with natural flavourings. Wild Thingz says its range contains half the sugar of leading UK sweet brands and contains no artificial colours or flavours. The promotion runs throughout October and is part of the brand’s wider ‘No Trickz. Just Treatz.’ campaign aimed at encouraging families to choose lower‑sugar confectionery. Besides Ocado, Wild Thingz products are stocked through Amazon, Whole Foods Market, Planet Organic, Center Parcs, Everyone Active, and independent retailers.
“Halloween is all about having fun, but we know the cost of all those little extras can quickly add up for families,” Fliss Newland, Founder of Wild Thingz said.
“We wanted to do something a bit wild this year – not just talk about making a better choice, but actually put the treats on us,” Fliss Newland, Founder of Wild Thingz said.
Wild Thingz makes plant‑based fruity sweets using natural flavourings and claims its range contains half the sugar of leading UK sweet brands. Alongside Ocado, the brand is stocked through Amazon, Whole Foods Market, Planet Organic, Center Parcs, Everyone Active, and a network of independent retailers.
Source: Grocery Gazette (https://grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/10/07/wild-thingz-launches-free-halloween-sweets-promotion-with-ocado)

item.title: Consumers limit AI agents’ payment access despite willingness to let them shop
item.description:
A PYMNTS Intelligence and Visa Acceptance Solutions survey of 1,185 merchants, 5,241 consumers and 150 acquirers found that 56% would let an AI agent search and compare products but only 35% would share saved payment credentials. For a $300 purchase, 52% of consumers want to pick the payment method themselves while 25% would accept an AI recommendation but retain final approval.
Ninety-six percent of surveyed acquirers say agent governance is important, and 93% say consent and data‑governance frameworks will be key to supporting agentic commerce.
While payment stacks have become fine-tuned for transaction authorization, agentic commerce inserts a new question.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/ai-agents-turn-permission-into-payments-new-control-point)

item.title: SoFi reports grocery trips up 13% as consumers manage cash flow
item.description:
SoFi Tech Solutions’ Q2 Debit Spend Index showed U.S. consumers increased grocery trips by close to 13% while cutting average basket size, according to senior director Max Spivakovsky. Fuel purchases jumped 28% and travel‑related spending rose 21% in the same period, indicating households kept discretionary spending despite higher essential costs.
Card‑on‑file transactions accounted for almost 25% of debit purchases and more than 30% of total debit spending in SoFi’s Q2 data. Those saved‑card purchases averaged close to $60, compared with an overall debit transaction average of $37. In SoFi’s research, about 20% of consumers said they would switch cards for better benefits, underscoring the demand for added value.
“Providers shouldn’t be just looking at isolated transactions anymore,” Max Spivakovsky said.
“When folks are feeling financially cautious, the absolute last thing they want to see is a surprise,” Max Spivakovsky said.
The article opens by noting that careful consumers are adjusting their spending without cutting overall outlays, using debit data to see how they juggle essentials and discretionary items. It cites SoFi’s Q2 Debit Spend Index as the source of the behavioral insights.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/consumer-payments/2026/careful-consumers-want-control-sofi-says-banks-should-hand-it-over)

item.title: Iceland launches rapid grocery delivery in 17 London stores ahead of Christmas
item.description:
Iceland has launched its Rapid Online Delivery service in 17 London stores ahead of the Christmas trading period. The service will expand to more than 200 stores across the UK before Christmas, starting with a wider London rollout from 19 October and reaching Manchester, Birmingham, and Liverpool from 26 October.
Customers can place orders through Iceland’s website or app, with delivery promised within an hour and some orders arriving in as little as 30 minutes. Iceland is offering free delivery on Rapid orders during the launch period to encourage trial. The service requires a minimum spend of £15 and excludes some large or bulky products. Orders are picked and packed by participating Iceland stores and handed to third-party delivery partners, allowing shoppers to track their order after dispatch.
“We understand that food plans can change at the drop of a hat. Whether it’s forgotten essentials for dinner, snacks for the kids’ packed lunches, or a craving you have to satisfy, shoppers can order with confidence knowing they can get what they need delivered at speed. That’s why we’ve launched our Rapid Online Delivery service, offering customers delivery within an hour,” Iceland spokesperson said.
Iceland already offers a nationwide next-day delivery service that is free on orders of £40 or more. Earlier this year, Iceland expanded its partnership with Amazon to make groceries available in Belfast, Cardiff, Edinburgh, and Nottingham.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/iceland-rolls-out-rapid-grocery-delivery-to-200-stores-ahead-of-christmas)

item.title: eBay releases 2026 Recommerce Report showing secondhand shopping grows worldwide
item.description:
eBay released its 2026 Recommerce Report on October 7, 2026, based on surveys of more than 10,500 consumers and more than 1,700 sellers across several markets. The report found that 70% of global consumers consider secondhand shopping important for managing their household budgets.
It also showed that 47% of respondents buy secondhand goods at least monthly, up from 35% in 2025.
“Recommerce has been core to our marketplace for 30 years, and this year’s report makes clear that its role in people’s lives is only growing,” Jamie Iannone, Chief Executive Officer at eBay said.
Source: eBay Newsroom (https://ebayinc.com/stories/news/ebay-recommerce-report-secondhand-shopping-rises-worldwide-as-consumers-seek-value-and-stretch-budgets)

item.title: UK retail media jumps 32% to £2bn in first half of 2026
item.description:
UK retail media spending rose 32% year-on-year to £2bn in the first six months of 2026, according to IAB UK’s Digital Adspend Study H1 2026. The growth outpaced the wider UK digital advertising market, which increased 13% to £21.2bn in the same period.
Video advertising climbed 18% to £5.1bn, while search remained the largest channel at £9.1bn after a 10% rise. Display advertising added 9% to reach £3.1bn, putting retail media ahead of gaming (£0.7bn), digital out‑of‑home (£0.5bn) and classified advertising (£0.5bn). The study also noted that 70% of advertisers cited economic uncertainty as a top challenge, with AI and automation (37%) and measurement (30%) following. Connected TV advertising via internet‑connected devices reached £1.7bn in H1 2026, up 22% year on year. Mediasense forecasts that UK digital advertising will grow 12% across 2026 to £45.2bn before moderating to 10.5% growth in 2027.
“Retail media’s 32% growth confirms that commerce data is no longer just a bottom-funnel targeting tool; it’s becoming a strategic layer across the whole customer journey,” Rob Ishag, UK country manager at TripleLift said.
Before this period, retail media was considered a fast‑growing niche, but the £2bn milestone shows it has become a major growth driver.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/retail-media-hits-2bn-as-uk-ad-spend-jumps-32-in-h1)

item.title: Six retailers named as finalists for 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
item.description:
John Lewis, Asda, Morrisons, H&M, Dunelm, and Waitrose were named finalists for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, with the ceremony set for Wednesday, 4th November. The organizers said they received a record number of entries for the 2026 awards.
The Bricks and Mortar Innovation shortlist includes pairs such as Dunelm with Enactor and Waitrose with SOLUM. Supply Chain Innovation features nominees like OneRail partnered with NVIDIA and THG Fulfil. Payments Innovation shortlist contains entries such as Edenred Payment Solutions with New Look and Justt with Madison Reed.
The 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards are sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027. The ceremony will take place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November, featuring a drinks reception, three-course meal, and an after‑party hosted by Aurie Styla.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/john-lewis-asda-morrisons-handm-dunelm-and-waitrose-among-2026-rtih-innovation-awards-finalists)

item.title: Christine Russo reports from Retail Club and Shoptalk Fall 2026
item.description:
Christine Russo reports from Retail Club and Shoptalk Fall 2026, noting Retail Club drew about 2,000 attendees this year. She also heard organisers expect more than 3,500 attendees at Shoptalk Fall in its third year and first Nashville edition. She surveyed over 50 attendees across both shows to gauge their impressions.
She observed that dense 1:1 meeting schedules pull participants off the main show floor, leaving the floor quieter and creating lulls in activity. Off‑premises vendor events are growing in size and number, further drawing people away from the hall. When sessions end, empty stages and dark voids with vacant chairs appear, resembling a party where the kitchen is full but the living room is empty. Russo suggests placing content on every stage throughout the day, even during meetups, to maintain intensity and keep attendees engaged.
Retail Club is in its second year, after a first year that brought roughly 500 attendees. Shoptalk Fall is entering its third year and is being held in Nashville for the first time. The organisers of Shoptalk anticipated more than 3,500 attendees for this edition.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/rtihs-american-correspondent-christine-russo-reports-from-retail-club-and-shoptalk-fall-2026)

item.title: Sainsbury’s names Sam Littlejohn, ex‑Amazon, as supply chain planning director
item.description:
Sainsbury’s has appointed Sam Littlejohn, formerly of Amazon, as its Director of Supply Chain Planning, noting he spent almost 11 years at the online retailer. It is rolling out RFID technology across about 400 TU clothing stores, aiming for completion by September. The 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony is set for Wednesday, 4th November at The HAC in Central London.
A pilot earlier this year demonstrated that RFID improved stock visibility, accelerated replenishment and enabled more efficient inventory management. The RTIH Innovation Awards have now closed for entries, with winners to be announced at the November ceremony. He noted that the ceremony marks the awards’ fifth year as a physical event, having grown from an initial gathering of 30 people to today’s record‑breaking attendance.
“This year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records,” Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH said.
The RFID roll‑out follows a trial conducted earlier this year in selected stores. Last year’s RTIH hall of fame inductees were unveiled at a sold‑out event on 16 October at The HAC, featuring a drinks reception, three‑course meal and an awards ceremony hosted by comedian Tiff Stevenson.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/sainsburys-raids-amazon-to-bring-in-sam-littlejohn-as-its-new-director-of-supply-chain-planning)

item.title: OAIC launches investigation into HeyCyan app maker Shenzhen Qingcheng
item.description:
Australia’s privacy regulator launched an investigation on Wednesday into Shenzhen Qingcheng Future Technology, maker of the HeyCyan smart glasses app sold through Big W Marketplace and Amazon. The OAIC said it had been monitoring smart‑glass rollout since early 2026 and, in August, received a request from the Attorney‑General to examine privacy implications. The regulator sought information from Meta, Kmart, Google and Shenzhen Qingcheng, but the China‑based firm did not respond.
The regulator asked manufacturers and distributors how the glasses record information, who can access that data and where it is stored. The move adds to growing scrutiny of camera‑equipped smart glasses in Australia, where the government said in September it was considering blocking their use in government workplaces over privacy and security concerns.
The OAIC said it had been monitoring the rollout of smart glasses since early 2026. In August it received a request from the Attorney‑General to examine the privacy implications of the devices.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/business/privacy-watchdog-probes-maker-of-smart-glasses-app-used-by-kmart-products-202610)

item.title: Apple blocks major ad tech firms in Safari via secret iOS 27 list
item.description:
Apple’s iOS 27 updates, released in mid‑September, began blocking major ad tech firms from tracking users in Safari. The initial list names The Trade Desk, LiveRamp, ID5, Permutive and Experian’s Audigent as blocked, while rivals such as Zeta’s LiveIntent, Lotame and Yahoo’s ConnectID remain unblocked. When a user opens Safari, the browser stops communicating with the blocked domains, preventing them from collecting data or serving ads.
Apple requires every browser installed on iPhone and iPad to use its WebKit engine, so Chrome, Firefox and others are subject to the same blocklist. The new WebKit code lets Apple add or remove companies from the list without waiting for a full iOS update, although the code has not yet shipped to users.
“What this will allow Apple to do is make this block list dynamic,” Rowena Lam, senior director of privacy and data at IAB Tech Lab and product lead for its Trusted Server initiative said.
Advertising Week New York, a four-day conference that draws nearly 20,000 of adland’s finest, is renowned for on-stage programming tinged with optimism and creator reps angling for their 15 minutes in the spotlight. However, out in the snaking lines outside the conference venue, nearby hotels and dive bars, the talk often circles back to Apple — the biggest brand/provider in the industry — which reopened its war with the digital ad industry just a week before.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media-buying/apples-secret-blocklist-is-the-talk-of-advertising-week-new-york-mostly-off-the-record)

item.title: Zara and Gap use luxury tactics to boost media impact and sales
item.description:
Zara and Gap are adopting luxury‑brand strategies such as designer partnerships to increase their media impact value, with Zara’s March 17 Galliano announcement delivering $8.3 million in MIV within 48 hours. Launchmetrics found that mass‑market brands employing premium tactics averaged twice the MIV of those that did not from January 2025 to June 2026.
Zara’s Bad Bunny Super Bowl look drove $19.9 million in MIV, according to Launchmetrics. GapStudio’s first full women’s collection, launched in April 2025, saw a $158 version of Anne Hathaway’s custom shirtdress sell out within hours. In the first half of 2026, 78 % of GapStudio’s MIV carried the theme ‘accessible elevation,’ while Zara’s Galliano announcement showed 62 % archival authority and 54 % premium elevation in its coverage.
“Longevity most often comes from what happens next [from the brand],” Alison Bringé, Launchmetrics’ chief marketing officer said.
“It brings brand awareness to a new generation,” Zac Posen, designer said.
Mass market brands have borrowed from luxury for decades, so the tactics themselves aren’t new, The wider Gap business is growing, too, in part through this designer association.
Source: Glossy (https://glossy.co/fashion/zara-gap-luxury-marketing-launchmetrics)

item.title: CPG brands face tariff‑financing mismatch after July U.S. tariff finalization
item.description:
In July, the U.S. Trade Representative set tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on goods from 60 trading partners, affecting nearly all U.S. imports. Founders of CPG brands earning $2 million to $20 million now see a working‑capital gap when tariffs shift after a retailer’s purchase order is locked. Retailers usually pay on 60‑ to 90‑day terms, leaving brands to finance the gap between co‑packer deposits and eventual receipt.
Brands often use short‑term debt or factoring that assumes steady costs, so a tariff rise mid‑cycle leaves them repaying debt based on the old price while absorbing the extra expense. Founders should model each order at current landed cost and again at 10%‑15% higher, then check whether their financing can absorb the swing without breaking cash flow.
Before the July tariff finalization, import‑dependent brands faced shifting duty rates that made cost forecasting difficult. The new fixed rates removed day‑to‑day volatility but still allow tariffs to be applied after a purchase order is priced.
Source: SupplyChainBrain (https://supplychainbrain.com/blogs/1-think-tank/post/44783-the-hidden-financing-risk-behind-the-new-tariff-environment)

item.title: Wayfair expands Klarna BNPL to offer 0% financing up to six months
item.description:
Wayfair and Klarna have expanded their buy now pay later partnership to give United States shoppers access to 0% APR financing for up to six months across Wayfair’s brand family. For Canadian shoppers, the deal marks the first time Klarna’s full suite of BNPL options is available at Wayfair, while shoppers can also pay in full or split purchases into interest‑free installments.
The 0% financing carries no interest and applies to purchases made through Wayfair, Joss & Main, AllModern, and Birch Lane. Shoppers in both countries can choose to pay the total amount at checkout, spread payments over several installments without interest, or finance larger orders over longer periods. The partnership renewal was announced by Klarna’s Chief Commercial Officer David Sykes and Wayfair’s Director Curtis Crawford.
“Wayfair's decision to renew and deepen this partnership speaks to the trust we've built together and the real demand we're seeing for flexible payments for considered home purchases,” David Sykes, Chief Commercial Officer at Klarna said.
“Klarna has been a trusted partner in helping our customers shop with confidence, and renewing this relationship was an easy decision,” Curtis Crawford, Director at Wayfair said.
The partnership expansion comes as the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards prepare to highlight payments innovation, with entries now closed and the ceremony set for 4 November at The HAC in Central London. Payments will be a key focus area at the awards, which celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast‑moving omnichannel world.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/wayfair-ramps-up-its-klarna-buy-now-pay-later-partnership-across-american-and-canadian-markets)

item.title: YEEP! hits 4,000 parcel lockers and prepares Generation 3 rollout
item.description:
YEEP! reported reaching 4,000 parcel locker locations across the UK in October 2026. It aims to expand to 5,000 lockers by the end of 2026.
All new lockers will use the Generation 3 specification from 2 November 2026. Existing units will be upgraded to Generation 3 by the end of Q1 2027. The lockers were developed with hardware partner kernTerminal and feature a bespoke operating system for network management.
“Reaching 4,000 locations is a big milestone for YEEP!, and the launch of Generation 3 gives us another reason to be excited about where the business is heading,” Jamie Dickinson, CEO said.
Before Jamie Dickinson became CEO in December 2025, YEEP! operated just over 2,250 parcel lockers. Since then the company has expanded to 4,000 locations and plans to reach 5,000 by the end of 2026.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/6/yeep-hits-4000-parcel-lockers-milestone-as-it-gears-up-to-roll-out-new-touchscreen-technology)

item.title: Wholesale and retail VAT trader count rose by 9,500 to 511,300 in 2024–25
item.description:
HMRC reported that the number of active VAT traders in the wholesale and retail sector increased by 9,500 to reach 511,300 in the 2024–25 fiscal year. This increase was the largest numerical gain across all sectors and meant wholesale and retail accounted for 22% of active VAT traders and £57bn of net Home VAT liability.
Across the whole UK VAT population, active traders grew by 11,400 to reach 2.33 million, meaning wholesale and retail contributed most of the net increase. The sector’s net Home VAT liability was £57bn, which was £1bn higher than the previous year. HMRC recorded 234,000 new VAT registrations and 218,000 deregistrations during 2024–25, showing substantial churn beneath the headline growth. The agency cautions that a rise in VAT traders does not equate to new shops opening or higher consumer demand, as businesses may register or deregister for reasons unrelated to retail activity. HMRC notes that the year‑end count of live traders was 2,285,900, while its annual active trader figure of 2.33 million includes anyone who filed a non‑nil VAT return at any point during the year.
HMRC’s latest annual VAT statistics, covering 2024–25 and updated in December 2025, provide a baseline for examining the registered trading population. HMRC’s figures reveal changes in the registered business population, but cannot alone establish whether retail sales or competitive pressure are rising.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/features/what-hmrcs-vat-data-reveal-about-the-changing-shape-of-uk-retail)

item.title: Suboo enters liquidation owing roughly $655,000
item.description:
Bondi‑founded fashion label Suboo collapsed into liquidation after a creditors meeting on October 1, reportedly owing about $655,000. It owes Shopify $140,232.89 and Wayflyer $105,162.50, among other debts.
The company also owes DHL $60,909.41, FedEx $58,299.49, Swell Ltd $51,840.66 and Dongguan P&J Clothing Co $18,253.25.; Founder Sue Di Chio began work on the brand in 2008, and Christopher Darin of Worrells was appointed sole liquidator per an ASIC notice.
Suboo stocks its products in stores such as Farfetch, Bloomingdale’s and Saks and says it appears in over 300 premium boutiques across 17 countries.; The brand said it has fulfilled all customer orders and maintains no unfulfilled purchases.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/sectors/fashion-accessories/celeb-favourite-suboo-enters-liquidation-owes-655000-202610)

item.title: California Governor Newsom Signs AB 1693 to Speed Storefront Permit Approvals
item.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed AB 1693 this week, granting retailers quicker access to permits for storefront improvements. Under the law, local building departments must review and approve or deny applications in 20 days or less.
Retailers making upgrades to existing buildings may hire qualified architects and engineers to certify that their plans meet structural and safety standards. The measure, sponsored by Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur, the California Retailers Association and WC3 Chambers of Commerce, a coalition of chambers in West Los Angeles, is part of a package that will take effect on January 1, 2027. Other legislation passed alongside AB 1693 includes the COMPETE Act, which provides novel protections against statewide monopolies, and AB 1679, which allows small businesses to open temporary pop-ups in empty retail locations and forego onerous permitting processes, as part of a broader set of small‑business bills. Newsom said the provision will make it easier and more attractive to do business statewide in California, according to the governor’s office.
“Retail is constantly changing, and brick-and-mortar businesses need to be able to change with it,” Rick Chavez Zbur, Assemblymember said.
“Retailers throughout California are vital contributors to their local economies, yet they continue to face lengthy local permitting processes across the state,” Rachel Michelin, President and CEO of the California Retailers Association said.
The measure also represents a feather in Newsom’s cap as he looks to entice California businesses to deepen their roots in the state.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/california-permits-storefront-improvements-newsom-ab1693-1239317427)

item.title: Shippers push for AI-capable 3PLs amid nearshoring surge and global disruptions
item.description:
According to the 2027 Third-Party Logistics Study released Tuesday, 74 percent of shippers report major or severe impacts from global conflicts and geopolitical disruptions. At the same time, 86 percent are increasing their use of outsourced logistics services while 74 percent are consolidating their 3PL partners, up from 50 percent in the prior year.
The study shows 93 percent of shippers deem AI important, very important or critical when choosing a 3PL, yet only 12 percent of providers say they are highly prepared to deliver AI-enabled operations. Nearshoring remains a priority, with 74 percent of shippers diversifying suppliers or sourcing regions and 73 percent raising safety stock or inventory buffers. Nike’s chief operating officer told employees the brand is shifting away from owning much of its fulfillment network and will focus more on local partnerships, reflecting the broader move toward regional sourcing.
“The preponderance of what we’ve been facing is a global reset in the geopolitical environment, supplemented by natural phenomena and, on top of that, a large driving force of global economic reset,” Mark Baxa, president and CEO of the Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals (CSCMP) said.
The research was produced by NTT DATA, Penske Logistics and the University of Tennessee’s Global Supply Chain Institute, with backing from the CSCMP. Anne Reinke of the Intermodal Association of North America pointed to a large increase in Mexico‑bound intermodal shipments. Bloomberg reported last week that Nike is pursuing a nearshoring strategy more aggressively than before.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/logistics/3pl-study-nike-nearshoring-ai-third-party-logistics-cscmp-penske-1239316246)

item.title: Fed and PYMNTS show stablecoin demand trails infrastructure growth
item.description:
Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and PYMNTS Intelligence reported that while 42% of middle-market firms have discussed or tested stablecoins, only 13% actually use them. The Cleveland Fed found that only 21 respondents said availability through a current financial provider would increase their interest in stablecoins. Among the eight Cleveland Fed respondents who are using or planning to use stablecoins, four said they would accept customer payments and four said they would pay suppliers.
PYMNTS Intelligence data shows that 88% of companies receiving stablecoins immediately convert them to U.S. dollars. These findings indicate that corporate curiosity about stablecoins outpaces actual deployment, highlighting a demand rather than supply issue. The Fed’s review of corporate disclosures found virtually no evidence that non‑financial, non‑crypto firms hold meaningful stablecoin balances on their balance sheets. The same Fed research showed that more respondents wanted proof that stablecoins were cheaper or more efficient, more time to watch adoption, or demand from customers or suppliers. All three that envisioned stablecoins serving a treasury function also intended to use them for payments.
Over the past year and a half, stablecoins have secured clearer regulation, gained more institutional backing, and seen improved infrastructure from banks, FinTechs and payment providers, yet adoption remains low.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/blockchain/2026/the-fed-and-pymnts-intelligence-agree-stablecoins-have-a-demand-problem)

item.title: New York Fed says global supply chain pressure index hits 1.28, four‑month high
item.description:
The New York Federal Reserve reported that its Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI) rose to 1.28 in September. The index was up from an upwardly revised 1.20 in August, which itself had been raised from an initial reading of 1.06.
The GSCPI gauges global supply chain conditions by integrating transportation cost data and manufacturing indicators, and the New York Fed has published it since 1997. A reading of zero indicates the index is at its long‑term average, while positive values signal higher pressure and negative values signal lower pressure. The index reached a recent peak of 1.81 in May and an all‑time high of 4.43 in December 2021. In July, Reuters noted that supply chain pressures had started to ease after a four‑year high earlier in the year, attributing the earlier spike to the U.S.–Iran conflict disrupting trade through the Strait of Hormuz. The index is calculated as standard deviations from an average value, according to a graph included in the index. The last time the GSCPI had a negative value, or lower‑than‑average global supply chain pressure, was November 2025, with the current estimate for that month at -0.21.
In September, Bloomberg reported that the Port of Los Angeles blocked more than 120 million cyberattacks during August, with its cybersecurity team identifying intrusion, network exploitation, credential harvesting and malware attacks. The port is described as America’s busiest container hub for global trade.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/supply-chain/2026/new-york-federal-reserve-reports-global-supply-chain-pressures-reach-4-month-high)

item.title: Retailers reshape associate roles as AI shifts in-store expectations
item.description:
Retailers are training store associates to confirm or suggest product additions in under a minute as shoppers arrive with AI-driven research. Shoppers often spend a couple hours or more researching products via AI before entering stores, raising expectations for associate expertise.
Training focuses on product knowledge that exceeds what generic AI tools can provide, especially for complex or expensive items. At big-box chains like Walmart, many shoppers prefer minimal associate interaction unless a problem arises, while specialty retailers rely on associates as trusted experts. Associates receive AI-based onboarding help, but brands must ensure they can answer questions quickly without external tools.
“Back then, store associates were saying, 'Customers come in, and they've already done all this research, and they know more about the products than I do because they have access to all this information that I don't have access to,',” Nikki Baird, vice president of strategy and product at Aptos Retail said.
“AI will only return answers for what you ask it,” Garry Heon, senior vice president and sector head of retail and consumer goods, communications, media and entertainment at QualityAI said.
Before AI, the spread of branded websites gave customers product information online, changing how associates interacted with shoppers in store.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/where-do-associates-fit-in-an-ai-world-retail/831640)

item.title: Autonomous trucks log 440,000 driverless miles on Sun Belt routes
item.description:
Aurora reported that its driverless trucks had logged close to 440,000 miles by the end of June 2025. It now operates on 10 driverless routes across the Sun Belt, including a roughly 1,000‑mile Fort Worth‑to‑Phoenix lane, and expects more than 200 driverless trucks in service by year‑end.
Kodiak had 35 driverless-powered trucks running in the Permian by the end of June, with over 40,000 cumulative hours of paid driverless operations. Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Waabi began hauling freight for Warp’s LTL network on the Dallas‑Houston corridor with an observer still in the seat, and Waabi said driverless runs on Volvo’s purpose‑built truck will start next year. Waabi also said it has cut the time to open a new lane from three months to three weeks to, on at least one lane, nothing at all. All deployments remain limited to highway middle‑mile moves in good weather, leaving dock work, yard maneuvers, breakdowns and customer‑side tasks to human drivers.
Prior to June 2025, Aurora had logged more than 250,000 driverless miles by January after launching commercial operations on the Dallas‑Houston corridor in April 2025. Kodiak had already placed 20 driverless trucks in the Permian at the end of the previous year and grew that fleet to 35 by June.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/the-autonomous-trucks-are-coming-for-the-lane-not-necessarily-for-your-business)

item.title: Moralve adopts Amazon’s Global Warehousing to cut shipments from 5 to 1
item.description:
Since its 2021 launch, Moralve has adopted Amazon’s Global Warehousing and Distribution to centralize inventory, cutting inbound shipments from 5 to 1. U.S. sales represent roughly 75% of Moralve’s revenue, prompting the brand to seek a simpler way to stock overseas markets.
Through GWD, Moralve stores goods in bulk near Chinese manufacturing hubs and can allocate inventory to the U.S., Canada, Germany, or the U.K. based on demand forecasts, enabling rapid replenishment as sales shift. The service replaced the need for three-to-five separate international shipments with one inbound flow and a single purchase order, reducing administrative overhead and freight costs. Inventory levels are visible in a dashboard, allowing Moralve to shift stock between markets as demand changes and helping the brand avoid overstocking or understocking in any single market. Lead times are also factored into replenishment planning, helping Moralve balance stock across regions.
“[Inventory] sits in China, and then depending on the demand and the forecast, you can maybe send more to U.S.A, send less to the U.K,” Mo Kuhail, co-founder and CEO said.
Before adopting GWD, Moralve faced fragmented supply chains that made small overseas shipments uneconomical for its suppliers. Amazon’s Global Warehousing and Distribution service, launched in 2025 and expanded with new capabilities in September, promised a centralized inventory pool reaching Canada and Germany by year‑end.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/why-one-brand-adopted-amazons-growing-inventory-replenishment-service/832260)

item.title: Target revives Simply Shabby Chic line, launching bedding Sunday at $20 start
item.description:
Target announced Tuesday that it is reintroducing the Simply Shabby Chic home collection, with an initial bedding and decor line set to appear in stores and online starting Sunday. A holiday-themed assortment will follow later this month, and items will start at $20, with most priced under $50.
The collection features floral prints and textures such as ruffles and eyelets, including comforters, quilts, duvets, sheets, shams, decorative pillows and throws. Simply Shabby Chic is an affordable offshoot of designer Rachel Ashwell’s Shabby Chic brand, which first appeared at Target in 2004. The relaunch aligns with Target’s broader merchandising overhaul, which has seen Cara Sylvester named chief merchandising officer and Isaac Mizrahi appointed creative director at large to guide product concepts and mentor the design team. Mara Sirhal said the return will please longtime fans while giving new shoppers a chance to discover the style for the first time. She also noted that the partnership reinforces Target’s goal to strengthen its merchandising authority in the home category through style, design and value.

“This partnership builds on our commitment to strengthen our merchandising authority in Home with style, design and value at the center,” Mara Sirhal, senior vice president of home merchandising at Target said.
Since Michael Fiddelke became CEO in February, Target has overseen a merchandising overhaul that included naming Cara Sylvester chief merchandising officer and bringing in additional senior vice presidents. The company also appointed Isaac Mizrahi as creative director at large to advise on product concepts and mentor the design team.

item.title: Lenders use alternative data to approve millions more borrowers
item.description:
Lenders are turning to bank‑transaction data, cash‑flow records and richer credit histories to approve loans for millions of U.S. adults who lack traditional scores. Recent underwriting shows that verified bank transactions can lift approvals by up to 8% for underserved segments, Affirm’s new model adds 3.4% more completed purchases, and Plaid’s LendScore delivers a 73% approval rate versus a 65% benchmark.
Roughly 25 million U.S. adults have insufficient recent credit activity to generate a usable score, according to the CFPB. About 35% of subprime consumers hold neither a credit nor a store card, compared with 12% of prime and 4% of super‑prime borrowers. Personify Financial reports that adding verified bank‑transaction data increased approvals by up to 8% among underserved consumers while keeping credit costs steady. Affirm’s latest transformer‑based underwriting model generated 3.4% more completed purchases at comparable risk by approving applicants its earlier system had declined. Plaid’s LendScore model posted a 73% approval rate versus 65% for a traditional benchmark at equivalent risk, and at the same approval rate it observed 41% lower risk. The Federal Reserve estimates that 32 million U.S. adults are unscoreable, including 7 million with no credit history and 25 million with thin files. PYMNTS Intelligence counts roughly 44 million U.S. adults as subprime, or 17% of consumers, with 55% living paycheck‑to‑paycheck and 19% using buy now, pay later services. For small‑business lenders, a survey of 350 executives found 57% citing inaccurate or incomplete business records as an underwriting obstacle, and microbusiness credit applications approved at a 77% rate versus 95% for large enterprises, with 19% rejected for insufficient information.
